collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: Asked for the best year of their life, a villager says the year their roof leaked: explain why, or refuse to say.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At the fire, someone has asked everyone, "What was the best year of your life?" People are giving the expected answers: the year they married, the year a baby came, the year of the great harvest. When it's (subject)'s turn, (subject.he/she) thinks for a moment and says, "The year my roof leaked."

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Everyone wants to know why. (subject) explains: (subject.his/her) roof leaked all year, so (subject.he/she) slept at a different friend's hut every few nights. (subject.He/she) has never laughed so much, eaten so many different dinners, or heard so many stories. (subject.He/she) finally fixed the roof and was a bit sad about it. (friend) says (friend.he/she) remembers (subject) sleeping over. "You snored," (friend.he/she) says. "So did you," says (subject).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Why?" says everyone. (subject) just smiles. "It was a very good year." (subject.He/she) won't say any more. People guess for weeks. (friend) is convinced it was a secret love affair. (villager) is sure (subject) found treasure. It was the roof. (subject) enjoys the guessing almost as much as (subject.he/she) enjoyed the year.
